question: A, B and C can do a piece of work in 3, 15 and 10 days, respectively. How long (in days) will they take to do twice the same work, working together?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM of 3, 15, and 10 = 30 units

Total efficiency (A + B + C) = (30 ÷ 3) + (30 ÷ 15) + (30 ÷ 10) = 10 + 2 + 3 = 15 units/day

Target work = 2 × Total Work = 2 × 30 = 60 units

Combined time taken = 60 ÷ 15 = 4 days

**∴ The correct answer is 4 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A = 3 days

Time taken by B = 15 days

Time taken by C = 10 days

**Formula Used:**

Time = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency

 
 

 **Person**

 **Efficiency**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total efficiency of A, B, and C together = 10 + 2 + 3 = 15 units/day.

⇒ Let the initial total work be 30 units.

⇒ New work required (twice the same work) = 2 × 30 = 60 units.

⇒ Time taken together = New work ÷ Total efficiency

⇒ Time taken together = 60 ÷ 15 = 4 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns

Works exactly like Time & Work. Inlet pipes have positive efficiency (filling) and outlet pipes have negative efficiency (emptying).

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the exact ratio of the work done by each person. If people work for the same number of days, wages are distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Alternate Days Work

When two people work on alternate days, find the combined work done in a "cycle" of 2 days, multiply the cycle close to total work, and then assign the remaining work to the first person.
